articles.title: Man City boss Maresca defends VAR after controversial Haaland derby goal
articles.summary: The VAR debate has raged since the Manchester derby, but Enzo Maresca says it wrongly overshadows City’s win at United
articles.body:
Manchester City manager ‌Enzo Maresca said the debate surrounding the VAR decision that awarded ⁠Erling Haaland’s winning ⁠goal against Manchester United should not overshadow his side’s 10-man performance in the 1-0 derby victory .

Haaland’s second-half strike on Sunday ⁠was initially ruled out for offside, but was awarded following a VAR review that judged the Norwegian to be onside. Refereeing body Pro ⁠Ref later acknowledged that VAR had been wrong to allow the decisive goal .

City were reduced to 10 men in the 23rd minute when Phil Foden was sent off for kicking out at Bruno Fernandes but held on to ‌secure the win.

“To talk about one moment after that game when we played for 70, 75 minutes with 10 players is quite poor. I think the performance was unbelievable and I’m pleased,” Maresca told reporters on Wednesday before Thursday’s League Cup third-round tie against Norwich City.

“There is knowledge that there was a mistake and that’s all. Sometimes, ⁠it goes for you. Sometimes, against you.”

The City ⁠boss also pointed to a controversial decision in a 2-1 defeat by Manchester United in January 2023, saying the club was still waiting for an apology after Fernandes scored despite ⁠Marcus Rashford being in an offside position.

Maresca was an assistant coach at City at the time.

“Three years ⁠ago when I was here, it happened the ⁠exact same against Manchester United. The goal was not a regular goal, and no one apologised. We are still waiting for the apology for that,” he said.

Maresca also defended the VAR ‌officials who, he said, often have little time to make difficult decisions and mistakes were, therefore, inevitable.

“Sometimes, they go for you, the decisions, sometimes, they go against you,” he said. “But also it’s not easy, I think, for the VAR, for the people that are in front of the screen, and in 10 seconds, 20 seconds they have to make a decision.

“It’s not easy for them. Sometimes, they make some mistakes. I make mistakes; players make mistakes; I think it’s part of our job.”

articles.title: Travis Kelce Named as Victim in Multi-Million-Dollar Fraud Scheme by Prosecutors
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs tight end was briefly named in court as Siddharth Jawahar 38, was sentenced to 11 years in prison on Tuesday, Sept. 15
articles.body:
Travis Kelce was named as a victim in a multi-million-dollar Ponzi scheme

Siddharth Jawahar, 38, was sentenced to 11 years in prison on Tuesday, Sept. 15, after misusing over $35 million from investors to fund an "extravagant" lifestyle and repay earlier investors

Kelce was reportedly linked through an investment fund co-founded by Jawahar but was only briefly mentioned in court

Travis Kelce has been named as a victim in a multi-million-dollar fraud scheme by prosecutors in a Missouri court, according to reports.

On Tuesday, Sept. 15, Siddharth Jawahar, 38, was sentenced to 11 years in prison, according to a press release from the U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri.

He pleaded guilty to three counts of wire fraud in January and has been ordered to pay more than $31 million in restitution to his victims after running a Ponzi scheme, the release noted.

According to outlets including KMOV and WENG , Kansas City Chiefs tight end Kelce was only briefly mentioned in court, and prosecutors did not expand on the 36-year-old's connection to the case.

A Forbes article published in 2021 states that Kelce was an investor in the Swiftarc Venture Labs Fund, created by Swiftarc Capital LLC, an investment company co-founded by Jawahar.

Jawahar ran the investment company Swiftarc Capital LLC and began investing client funds in a single investment, Philip Morris Pakistan, in 2015, per the press release. However, when the value of the investment declined, he didn't tell the investors, instead claiming they were making profits.

The Swiftarc Ventures Labs Fund was listed in the release as one of several additional entities he used in his scheme.

From around July 2016 through December 2023, Jawahar took in more than $35 million from investors but only invested about $10 million. He used money from new investors to repay older investors and to finance his "extravagant" lifestyle, the release stated.

His lifestyle included "travel on private jets, stays at luxury hotels, a luxury apartment in Austin and New York City, memberships at multiple private clubs across the country, spending sprees at clothing stores and expensive outings at fancy restaurants."

After he was indicted, Jawahar tried to "coach" a victim into giving a "favorable" statement to the FBI, which investigated the case, and tried to get his sister to remotely wipe his iPhone to hide evidence and lied about his immigration status, according to the release.

PEOPLE reached out to the U.S. Attorney's Office, Eastern District of Missouri, and representatives for Travis Kelce for comment.

articles.title: Las deportistas españolas critican el anuncio de Sydney Sweeney: "Nuestro cuerpo no es el espectáculo"
articles.standfirst: Lourdes Mohedano, Ona Carbonell, Sara Hurtado, Eva Moral o Desi Vila reivindican que el deporte femenino merece ser visto por lo que son capaces de hacer
articles.summary: Lourdes Mohedano, Ona Carbonell, Sara Hurtado, Eva Moral o Desi Vila reivindican que el deporte femenino merece ser visto por lo que son capaces de hacer
articles.body: Las deportistas españolas también han alzado la voz ante el anuncio de la actriz Sydney Sweeney para una plataforma de apuestas deportivas. La protagonista de La asistenta o de la serie Euphoria aparece desnuda mientras simula practicar varios deportes y se tapa el cuerpo con algunos objetos deportivos (bate de béisbol, guantes de boxeo, balones de fútbol americano...). Las primeras reacciones llegaron de deportistas olímpicas británicas, australianas o americanas como Ariarne Titmus, Gracie Kramer o Tilly Kearns, todas ellas criticando la sexualización del deporte femenino. Desde España también han surgido voces que critican el rol de Sweeney en esta campaña. La exgimnasta Lourdes Mohedano, plata olímpica en Río 2016, publicó un vídeo en su cuenta de Instagram en el que se muestra tajante: "Tenemos resistencia, potencia, velocidad, fuerza. Somos deportistas. Por eso me parece una vergüenza que, en un ámbito donde todavía nos cuesta que se reconozca nuestro trabajo y se nos tome en serio, sigamos recurriendo a la sexualización de la mujer". "No solo somos un cuerpo, somos atletas. En el deporte se merece que se hable de nuestro esfuerzo, de nuestro rendimiento, de nuestros resultados y lo que hay detrás de una deportista. Nuestro cuerpo no es el espectáculo, pero lo que somos capaces de hacer sí", explica Mohedano. El mensaje de Mohedano ha encontrado el respaldo de otras deportistas españolas que lo han aplaudido. Es el caso de la patinadora Sara Hurtado ("Cortita y al pie. Así es, compañera. Y así se habla") o la gimnasta Polina Berezina ("Grande. Nada más que añadir"). Ona Carbonell también publicó un vídeo con un contundente mensaje: "Sydney, me costó mucho entender que no sólo somos un cuerpo. Somos fuertes, somos rápidas, somos valientes, somos capaces". Con el acompañamiento de la canción 'Training Season' de Dua Lipa, que se ha convertido en la banda sonora de estos mensajes de las deportistas femeninas en todo el mundo. Eva Moral, triatleta paralímpica, también publicó en su Instagram un mensaje en Instagram: "Esto también es el cuerpo de una mujer en el deporte. Un cuerpo que entrena, compite, cae, se levanta y lucha por superarse cada día. El deporte femenino merece ser visto por lo que somos capaces de hacer, no por cómo nos vemos haciéndolo". Unas palabras que acompaña con un vídeo en el que se la ve entrenando y compitiendo. Su compañera Desi Vila, atleta paralímpica, también publicó un vídeo de ella entrenando siguiendo la campaña lanzada en redes por otras deportistas bajo el lema: "Así luce una mujer en el deporte".

articles.title: 6 NHL Landing Spots for Hurricanes' Alexander Nikishin After Revealed Trade Request
articles.summary: According to The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun as of Monday, Hurricanes defenseman and RFA Alex Nikishin is "not backing off" from his trade request.
articles.body:
According to The Athletic's Pierre LeBrun as of Monday, Hurricanes defenseman and RFA Alex Nikishin is "not backing off" from his trade request.

The 24-year-old, who remains unsigned, was drafted at No. 69 in 2020 and was a highly touted prospect before joining the Canes during the 2024-25 playoffs. Now he's got his first regular season and a Cup-winning playoff run under his belt, but the Hurricanes are so stacked on the blue line that there hasn't been much space for Nikishin to evolve.

Nikishin has shown potential and deserves a shot at quarterbacking a power play and a bigger opportunity overall than the Canes can currently give him, so a change of scenery is for the best overall.

Which teams could give him the shot to develop into one of their best defensemen?

The Flames made a major move to shore up their defense and accelerate their rebuild when they traded for Simon Nemec, a former No. 2 overall Devils pick. Could Nikishin be the next edition that takes them into their long-awaited future?

They're swimming in cap space and would be able to dish out the raise the RFA is expecting. They've got a huge hole on their left side, where Nikishin naturally plays, and this could provide some healthy competition with Nemec as both vie for the No. 1 power play quarter back spot.

Plus, he'd be a great complement to top Flames defenseman of the future, Zayne Parekh. If Nikishin is seeking a true opportunity to play big minutes and become "the guy," the answer could be Calgary.

The Predators are at a crossroads, and they finally went in a new direction by naming savvy former Avalanche brass Chris MacFarland as the new GM. MacFarland has already made a few splashes, like acquiring Ross Colton and Jack Drury from his former team.

Could Nikishin make sense as another big structural change here? The Predators have some newly acquired draft capital to toss around, which seems like the answer for the Hurricanes, who don't want to take on too much cap space in any potential deal.

The Flyers had a thrilling, if unexpected, trip to the playoffs last season, but they'll have to build on that roster and keep increasing the talent around Porter, Martone, and Trevor Zegras if they're to maintain last season's success and/or take the next step. They attempted to do this by tendering Leo Carlsson an offer sheet, but it was famously matched by his home team, the Ducks.

Now the Flyers clearly have tons of cap space and aren't afraid to use it. They certainly could use more scoring and skill on defense — particularly on the left side. Nikishin would join the likes of Jamie Drysdale and Cam York as the younger defensive core in Philly shapes up.

The Blues are another team on this list looking to continue fleshing out talent around a younger core. St. Louis finally parted ways with Jordan Kyrou in a difficult — but probably necessary — commitment to working on their future.

Highly skilled Philip Broberg is the Blues' best defenseman and will stay on the first pairing on the left side, but Nikishin could slot into the second pairing. In this situation, he'd still upgrade from the Hurricanes' third line, play bigger minutes, and have an opportunity to quarterback the top power-play unit.

This would be an option where both sides could feel comfortable easing into a less risky jump in minutes for Nikishin.

When it comes to the 2026-27 Vancouver Canucks, the question will be "why not?" in every sense of the word. The rebuild is on , and there is time, space, and money to explore upgrades at every position on the ice.

With the Canucks, Nikishin would truly want to ask himself if the bigger role and better opportunity as an individual player are worth the sacrifice of a few years of missing the playoffs. He is coming off of a Stanley Cup win, after all.

If the Canucks are willing to invest in the 24-year-old, it could pay off down the line when he is still in his prime and the tides start turning for the team overall. Worst-case scenario, they flip him to a more competitive team for different assets if it doesn't work out later.

The Winnipeg Jets have the hockey world ablaze right now as we await the aftermath of Connor Hellebuyck's trade request.

Acquiring Nikishin seems unlikely from a cap standpoint, and unfortunately, for them, unloading Hellebuyck doesn't do much to alleviate cap concerns.

Still, if they're going to be without the best goaltender in the world, they'll want to shore up their defense. He won't win the No. 1 spot on the left side, which belongs indefinitely to Josh Morrissey, but he will provide competition on the second and third pairings with left-siders Dylan Samberg and Mario Ferraro.

It's unclear exactly where the Jets are headed, but a player like Nikishin could help them stay competitive if they intend to make it back to the playoffs, or he could make a rebuild less painful if that's where the Jets want to take this.

articles.title: Ollie Millroy thanks Loek Hartog for saving him from his burning car
articles.summary: British racing driver Ollie Millroy says it is a "miracle I'm alive" after fellow driver Loek Hartog "did everything right" when saving him from his blazing car.
articles.body:
British racing driver Ollie Millroy says it is a "miracle I'm alive" after fellow driver Loek Hartog saved him from his car when it was engulfed in flames.

Millroy, 36, was hit by two other cars during the China GT Championship race at the Shanghai International Circuit 11 days ago, with his Ferrari immediately catching fire before hitting the safety barriers.

A barely conscious Millroy was stuck in his car for over a minute before he was pulled from the burning wreckage by Dutchman Hartog after he immediately stopped his car to help him.

"He acted instantly and he did everything right," a recovering Millroy told BBC Sport from his hospital bed in China.

"Watching the video back, it looks like you're watching a movie and everything's rehearsed.

"He ran around to check on me and realised the fire was too bad, and went round to the passenger side and realised he wasn't going to get me out of there; got an extinguisher, kept the fire off me for long enough to get inside the car and get me out of it.

"Every single step was perfectly executed. If you look at the photos and videos of the car, the fact I've got out without life-changing burns or even the fact I'm alive - it's a miracle.

"It was as though it was meant to be," added Millroy. "I'm not religious in any way, but it was as though someone had pre-programmed him to get me out of that car.

"It's created this really strong bond between us. I didn't have any memory of the crash, the first time anyone talked me through it was Loek in the hospital and the two of us were just in floods of tears when he was telling me what happened and what [he] did and how different the result could have been for me."

Millroy, who suffered several fractures and a punctured lung in the impact, says he has no memory of just before and for about an hour after the accident, which is affecting him psychologically as he tries to piece together what happened.

"It's a strange feeling - I'm still not coming to terms with it because I don't remember any of it. I was sort of conscious; I was talking to Loek and I took my helmet off because I had run out of oxygen and I was struggling to breathe.

"But I wasn't getting myself out of the car. My body had gone into some sort of survival mode because of the amount of the injuries I'd sustained.

"Watching the video is like I'm watching something else. I keep waking up at night where my brain is trying to piece together what happened to my body - that frustration seems to be building more and more."

Millroy eventually intends to continue racing, but first he is set to be reunited with Hartog, 23, as the Dutchman flies back to China this week so the pair can meet for the first time since the day of the crash.

"I remember being scared very briefly," says Hartog, who races a Porsche for various different teams across GT racing.

"I tried to run to the car and I was seeing if he was making an effort himself and quickly realised it was a one-sided quest. I saw I needed to free the space around him to get out [of the car]."

By the time he saw the scene Millroy's car was already stationary, and Hartog recalled that it was another 59 seconds from when he stopped his car to Millroy exiting his burning vehicle.

"I wish it were sooner," Hartog said. "There's a human element to that. I don't know why I went there; why I chose [to help him]. There was no reasoning, and I explain to myself that it was how I have been taught - how I grew up in some way."

Millroy's wife Fern has been by her husband's side since hours after the crash, with the couple's three children being looked after by Fern's sister.

"It's so emotional. I feel like I need that closure to give [Hartog] a great big hug," she said.

"It's incredible how you can instantly love someone you've never met before - we've probably been around the same paddocks over the years, but to love someone who has just taken care of my soulmate and father of our three children, it's incredibly significant."

Millroy joked: "I'm just sorry I can't take him out anywhere nicer for dinner [when they meet] but I'm tied to machines in the hospital bed.

"We've got to know Loek's parents and you can see how he's come from the most wonderful, amazing family, and that you don't have to be a bad guy to be a great sportsman; you can be a really nice guy and really good sportsman.

"He made a decision that day he was going to prioritise something else other than sport, and that's what saved my life."

While Hartog wants to "close their chapter" by revisiting Millroy in China, the pair expect to work closely together in the future - in particular on matters of safety.

"There'll always be an element of risk," says Millroy. "But we always take that for granted.

"I never got in that car on that day and thought: 'I really hope there's a highly trained and expert fire crew down that corner in case something happens.'

"I don't want to comment too much until it's been officially investigated. There's a lot of people wanting a lot of answers."

Hartog adds: "This specific moment is something we can use to make the sport safer - there was a multitude of things that went wrong: I shouldn't have been the person to help but if it weren't for me, the outcome could have been very different."

Millroy added: "As soon as I feel ready I want to get back in the car, but I've not been home yet, not seen the kids - there's a lot of things I want to go through in my head first.

"I must have said 'thank you' a thousand times and I'd say it another thousand times that I'm so unbelievably grateful. All the emotions won't make sense until I get back home with the kids and then it'll be like: 'OK, I am actually still alive and living my life.'

"There was a very good chance that wasn't going to happen if it wasn't for Loek."

articles.title: Cody Rhodes Reveals The Rock Pitch, Bronson Addresses Oba Controversy, Sami Zayn Praises CM Punk
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Rhodes Talks Idea for 'Soul' Storyline with The Rock

Penta's Time as WWE Champion Is Coming 👀

During a conversation Wednesday with The Rock's daughter, Simone Johnson, Cody Rhodes revealed that he had an idea to involve her in his storyline with The Final Boss last year.

Leading up to Elimination Chamber 2025, The Rock made a proposal to Rhodes, asking Cody to give him his soul. Rhodes famously declined, resulting in John Cena shockingly turning heel by attacking The American Nightmare at Elimination Chamber.

Speaking Wednesday on the What Do You Wanna Talk About podcast (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), Rhodes discussed the pitch he made regarding Simone's involvement.

"When he asked me for my soul, I thought, you know what would've been funny? Is to relent and give my soul, but not to him," Rhodes said. "And this is at the time when you were the NXT general manager, to you. And I thought, that's got legs. I'll never say a word again. She'll speak."

Both Rhodes and Johnson expressed their belief that they would have "crushed" the storyline, but it never got off the ground since Cody never actually presented it to The Rock.

Had Rhodes done so, Johnson expressed her belief that her father would have been open to the idea, saying, "I think he would've been all for it."

While Johnson is no longer with WWE, she was at the time of the "soul" storyline, as she performed under the name Ava in NXT.

Ava was the NXT general manager, giving her an authoritative presence that at least a portion of the WWE audience would have been familiar with.

However, coming out of Elimination Chamber 2025, essentially all of the focus was on Rhodes and Cena, as The Rock removed himself from the feud and allowed them to get the spotlight.

Had Rhodes pitched his idea and gotten Ava to be part of the storyline, though, it is fair to wonder if that would have kept The Rock around for the entirety of the WrestleMania 41 build.

Reed Addresses Controversial Segment with Oba

Bronson Reed brushed off the controversy surrounding his segment with Oba Femi from last week's episode of Raw.

After Reed made his surprise return from injury at Sunday Night's Main Event, he and the rest of The Vision brutally attacked Femi last week on Raw.

At the end of the onslaught, Reed put his foot on a prone Femi, only for The Ruler to shove Reed's foot off of him.

During an interview this week with The West Sport (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), Reed chalked up Oba's reaction to competitive spirit and the desire to be the top guy.

"Well, I think you've got to remember, like, I am the top dog," Reed said. "I'm always going to assert dominance and that's what I would try to do and he's very much the same. That's why he obviously hit my foot off, like, so if people have speculation about these things, then go for it. Speculate, but of course, like, both of us want to be number one and we're going to do whatever it takes to be number one."

Coming out of that Raw, WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats) reported that Oba's reaction to Reed's pose was not scripted.

WrestleVotes added that some people within WWE were not happy with the way Femi handled the situation.

There don't seem to be any hard feelings on Reed's part, though, which suggests he and Oba should have no issue working together in their rivalry moving forward.

Femi still has unfinished business with Bron Breakker after their SNME match ended in a disqualification, but everything seems to be building toward an eventual one-on-one clash between Bronson and Oba as well.

On the heels of beating CM Punk for the WWE Championship last week on SmackDown, Sami Zayn gave his rival some credit this week.

During an appearance on Busted Open (h/t WrestlePurists ), Zayn noted that although he has had his doubts about Punk over the years, he has been impressed with his in-ring work.

"Phony? Yeah. Overrated? I have to be honest, I never got in the ring with him until earlier this year, and I can't take it away from him," Zayn said. "He's great in the ring. He actually opened my eyes because for a long time, the hype around Punk was like… you can say the same thing about me because people have said it about me. They're like, 'I don't get this guy.' And there were times that Punk, to the levels he reached, I was like, 'I don't get how he reached these levels.' Clearly, there is something about him, but I didn't always get the hype.

"But after I got in the ring with him three or four times this year, you can't take it away from him. Trust me, I would love to. I would love to just sit here and bash him for the next 10-15 minutes. But in the ring, I can't take it away from him."

Just nine days after Zayn won the WWE title for the first time, he dropped it to a returning Punk on the July 6 episode of Raw in Punk's hometown of Chicago.

Zayn had been angling for a rematch ever since then, and he finally got it last week on SmackDown in Mexico City.

It was a chaotic bout that saw Johnny Gargano, Candice LeRae and Kevin Owens all get involved. Owens meant to hit Zayn with the WWE title belt after Zayn previously cost him in his title match against Punk, but he accidentally hit Punk instead.

That led to Sami pinning and defeating Punk, making him the 33rd different Superstar in WWE history to hold the WWE Championship at least twice.

Given how last week's match went down, the rivalry between Zayn and Punk is likely far from over, and Zayn's comments suggest he may be fine with that.

articles.title: Max Verstappen Beats 100 Go-Kart Drivers in Red Bull F1 Star's 'Max vs. 100' Challenge
articles.summary: It turns out being one of the most successful F1 drivers of all-time also makes you good at go-kart driving, as Max Verstappen proved on Wednesday.
articles.body:
It turns out being one of the most successful F1 drivers of all-time also makes you good at go-kart driving, as Max Verstappen proved on Wednesday.

Starting from the back of the pack against 100 go-kart drivers in what was dubbed the "Max vs. 100" challenge, Verstappen jumped up 64 spots into 37th place just on the first lap of the race.

Verstappen did wait until the eighth lap until he got into the top three, giving him 22 laps to move into first place. He finally ended it roughly 35 minutes after it started.

He also made it clear throughout he had no interest in treating this like an exhibition.

Red Bull, Verstappen's team since 2016, organized the event that required him to start 101st in the 101-driver field. He then had 30 laps to overtake the field with competitors being eliminated and sent to the pit area when he passed them.

"A hundred is a lot, you know, but I think how they've set up the track from what they've shown me, I think it will be good," Verstappen told ESPN's Laurence Edmondson prior to the race. "But it's still going to be hectic, for sure."

The 100 drivers challenging Verstappen were comprised from a group of Red Bull athletes, content creators, journalists and fans from around the world.

y doubt about Verstappen being able to win was immediately erased on the first lap. He finally got to the front of the pack on the 14th lap.

The only reason it took as long to finish the race is because you don't really get a sense of how far back in the field the 101st kart is until you see it and the chaotic mess that was the start of the event.

Verstappen told Edmondson it would be "quite embarrassing" if he was unable to win.

"I'm hoping that with my background, I should be faster than most. I hope! I mean, it would be quite embarrassing if they're faster than me!"

No one was even close to being faster than Verstappen, who scored his first win of the season. The 28-year-old has made the podium six times in 14 F1 races, including four in his last five events.

Perhaps Wednesday's go-kart showing will be the thing that helps propel Verstappen forward and into the winner's circle at his day job.

articles.title: Raiders HC reveals Brock Bowers practice update with Week 2 hope
articles.summary: The Raiders' star tight end isn't ready just yet, but there's some hope.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders played Week 1 without Brock Bowers and wound up beating the Miami Dolphins without him. It was a convincing win, and looking ahead to Week 2, the Raiders are hoping Bowers comes back.

But before his return, Bowers will need to suit up in practice, get some reps, and prove he's healthy enough to play in the upcoming Week 2 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers .

According to Sam Warren of The Athletic , Klint Kubiak told reporters that Bowers will not practice on Wednesday, but that there is hope he'll practice ahead of Week 2, potentially indicating a return this week is on the table.

Raiders get Brock Bowers update amid injury issue

"Klint Kubiak said Brock Bowers and Darien Porter won't practice today," Warren reports. "Hopes they will practice this week."

Bowers missed Week 1 against the Dolphins due to a knee issue, and his Week 2 status is still up in the air. This update brings both some good and some bad news.

On one hand, Bowers isn't practicing on Wednesday, which is a little bit concerning, though veterans typically get Wednesday off even if they're fully expected to play that week.

But seeing Bowers not out there is still a little worrisome. Then the further report that the Raiders are hoping that Bowers will practice before Week 2 is a good sign.

While he might not actually suit up in Week 2 for the Raiders, the fact that he seemingly has a realistic chance of practicing leading up to the second week of the season is a good sign for his status going forward.

Michael Mayer took the starting tight-end reps in Bowers' absence, and while he might have that same starting role in Week 2, Bowers at least is closing in on a return based on this report.

His practice reports later this week will tell whether he's set to play in Week 2, or maybe even in Week 3. For now, it's some good news, as the hope from the Raiders is a sign of things going in the right direction.

articles.title: Verstappen needs 35 minutes to pass 100 karts at Silverstone and win Red Bull challenge
articles.summary: Max Verstappen needed about 35 minutes to overcome 100 karting drivers in a Red Bull event at Silverstone on Wednesday.  Verstappen started 101st at the Silv...
articles.body:
SILVERSTONE, England (AP) — Max Verstappen needed about 35 minutes to overcome 100 karting drivers in a Red Bull event at Silverstone on Wednesday.

Verstappen started 101st at the Silverstone karting circuit, and overtook 64 drivers on the first lap alone, with many of his opponents crashing among themselves.

Many got blocked on the track after a pile-up that prompted a full-course yellow flag. Verstappen went off track but was able to return.

"That was simply lovely," Verstappen said. "It was a lot of fun."

Verstappen, who finished second in Formula 1's Spanish Grand Prix on Sunday, was up to 37th after the first lap, and up to sixth place by the sixth lap.

He went off track again but stayed comfortably faster than most drivers, none of them with any significant professional driving experience.

He said jokingly that the victory ranked as "the best one yet" in his career.

articles.summary: Michigan Football is heavily recruiting 2028 in-stater Marquis Ray, who’s now visited Ann Arbor for both home games this season:
articles.body:
One of the top athletes in the state of Michigan has now visited Ann Arbor for both home games this season. This recruit has yielded an offer since the summer and also holds legacy ties to the program.

Marquis Ray, the two-way star for Saline (Mich.) High, is the son of Marcus Ray. His first fall campaign with the Ann Arbor suburban school after transferring from central Ohio has led to him providing an instant impact to the MHSAA Division I juggernaut.

"I feel like things have been great. We're in a good defensive scheme and offensive scheme," Ray told Maize n Brew. "We're just a great team, and I could see us going far. I think I've been doing great. I've been good at man-to-man coverage. I've been covering my zones, breaking on the ball, triggering when I see the run, and just trying to make as many plays as I can."

Other Power 4 teams like Kentucky, Illinois and Pitt are showing strong interest in Ray, as this fall will be his opportunity to closely evaluate best fits with those being considered. For the Wolverines, the wins over WMU and Oklahoma were his chance to dive deep on schemes.

"They're real dominant," Ray said. "They play with some swag and confidence and I see myself like that."

Since the new coaching staff, led by Kyle Whittingham, entered the fray, Ray has also spent these past several months relationship building. He was offered in June after taking part in a camp hosted at Schembechler Hall, where he got to work with cornerbacks coach Jernaro Gilford and safeties coach Tyler Stockton.

"I think they're great coaches, they develop great DBs," Ray said. "I've seen coach Gilford at Utah. He's brought some pretty good DBs over."

As conversations continue between both sides, Ray hopes to show the staff his ability to tackle, cover and play any position in the secondary. Essentially, wherever he's needed, he'll be ready.

"I'm looking for a good relationship," Ray said. "If the school would actually wants me and wants to keep recruiting me, instead of just being like, 'Hey, come to the game.' Maybe if you're not going to offer me, I really shouldn't go there because the clock is ticking."

Ray, listed as the No. 17 overall 2028 in-state recruit by 247Sports, said a decision could come by the winter or potentially earlier. Before it does transpire, he'll keep hearing from one of his Saline teammates in 2027 offensive lineman commit Louis Esposito about coming aboard.

articles.title: ESPN’s Buccigross Sees Moritz Seider as Detroit’s Next Captain
articles.summary: ESPN's John Buccigross says Moritz Seider is going to be Detroit's next captain. #RedWings
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings stripped Dylan Larkin of the captaincy on Sept. 11 , and the team said it will open the 2026-27 season without naming a replacement. Lucas Raymond and Moritz Seider stay on as the alternate captains.

Training camp opens Wednesday, and Seider's name keeps coming up as the favorite to take the C whenever Detroit gets around to handing it out. One national voice is not waiting for the announcement.

John Buccigross Expects Moritz Seider to Be the Next Captain

John Buccigross, an NHL analyst at ESPN, was on the Spittin' Chiclets podcast with Paul Bissonnette talking through the Larkin situation. Buccigross does not think the next part is much of a mystery.

"Seider is going to be the captain, let's face it. He's the guy they're going to put the image, you know, the image and likeness of the Red Wings is him, and that's what they want everybody to be like. Like when it was Lidstrom back in the day and Yzerman back in the day, that's who they want to be like, is him."

It Would Be Detroit's First Defenseman With the C Since Lidstrom

Nicklas Lidstrom wore the C in Detroit from 2006 to 2012 , and every captain since has been a forward. Seider is 25 with a long NHL career in front of him. If the Red Wings hand him the letter, he would be the first defenseman to captain the franchise since Lidstrom retired.

articles.title: The Parker Report: How the Cowboys defense fared in week 1
articles.summary: Time to move on from last week.
articles.body:
With NFL Week 1 in the books, lets take a look at how first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker and his revamped defense looked against the Giants.

In their first week of action, the Cowboys defense gave up 394 total yards, 29 first downs, and allowed an 82% third down conversion rate (9/11). The team recorded two sacks and took advantage of one turnover on a forced fumble. The real gut punch here is the quantity of turnover worthy plays on defense (five) while only walking away with just the one.

The main storyline is of the game, however, is time of possession. The Giants offense was also their best defense, as they controlled the ball for over 36 minutes. The inability of the Cowboys defense to get off the field kept Dak and the high powered offense on the sideline, seeing the field just twice in the second half.

Second-year edge Donovan Ezeiruaku had one of the better nights on defense. He led the team with ten tackles, had a half sack, two hits on the quarterback, and one forced fumble.

Caleb Downs was the only player to finish with a full sack on the stat sheet. The quarterback takedown came on a well disguised slot blitz. The devastating blind side hit forced a Jaxson Dart fumble, conveniently landing in the waiting arms of a Giants offensive lineman. This was exactly the playmaking ability Downs showcased throughout his time at Alabama and Ohio State.

Speaking of fumbles, the team forced four of them but only recovered one. Donovan Ezeiruaku, Caleb Downs, Cobie Durant and Quinnen Williams each had their turn jarring the ball loose. The lone fumble recovery came on the Quinnen Williams punchout, which bounced right into Shavon Revel 's lap.

The Cowboys rolled out their 3-4 base on 28 snaps (41.2%), allowing 112 yards. They lined up in nickel on 24 snaps (35.3%) but allowed a whopping 215 yards. It's interesting to see that the extra DB is what spurred the leaky defense.

The coverage split was 77.8% zone and 22.2% man. Dallas lived in a two-high or three-deep zone structure throughout most of the day.

The Cowboys blitzed at the seventh highest rate in week one, but that translated to just the 21st ranking in pressures. And when Dallas rushed only four, Jaxson Dart went 17-of-19 for 200 yards and two touchdowns.

Dallas bit hard on the play-action. Dart was 5-of-7, had a touchdown, and ran for 26 yards on off the play fake. The young edges consistently crashed hard, opening outside lanes for Dart on the rollout pass or to take off and run.

Caleb Downs played nearly every snap on defense. The young star made his presence known with a huge hit on Jaxson Dart, forcing a fumble that was recovered by the Giants. His final stat line would read eight tackles, one sack, one forced fumble, and one QB hit. Where he could improve would be his pass coverage win rate. Great start for the rookie, but there is still much improvement to be had.

Malachi Lawrence was not good enough. He was involved in more than one negative big play on Sunday night. Too many times we saw him bite on play fakes, crashing down while leaving a huge void to the outside. His pass rush was nearly non-existent. Lawrence ended the night as the fourth lowest rated player on defense against the Giants.

Jaishawn Barham finished the night with six tackles as a rotational linebacker. He had one noticeable hit in the backfield, but outside of that was somewhat forgettable. There were questions about his effort late in the game as the Giants connected in the flat multiple plays in a row on their way to a game sealing touchdown. With Overshown potentially missing up to two weeks , we should see more of Barham against the Commanders and Ravens .

LT Overton played a small role Sunday night but did finish with one tackle and one pass breakup at the line. With a strong preseason and a solid first game with limited snaps, expect to see his role grow as the season continues.

The Cowboys came into MetLife Stadium with high expectations surrounding a fresh start on a rebuilt defense. What the Cowboys got was more of the same. There is no nice way to put this: this team was dominated on the defensive side of the ball. While they limited the explosive plays of over 15 yards, they allowed the Giants offense to methodically work their way down the field for touchdowns while chewing up so much clock that their own offense saw the field just twice in the second half.

We witnessed large voids in coverage more than once, resulting in touchdowns and first downs. Some mental mistakes are to be expected for a new defense, but too many of the same misses can be seen on film. Dallas will need to get this corrected in a hurry if they want to keep pace in the NFC.

The only reason this defense doesn't get an F is because they forced four fumbles. The law of averages did not apply as the ball seemed magnetized to Giants players after being stripped on more than one occasion. If the Cowboys can tighten up but also keep their intensity around punchouts and strip sacks, the football will bounce their way and win them some games.

The Cowboys have a ton of work to do on the defensive side of the ball. Their next test comes at home against the Washington Commanders this Sunday. Jaxson Dart's mobility was crucial for the Giants victory and Dallas faces another one coming to town in Jayden Daniels . It's imperative this defense doesn't overcommit to the inside play fakes because Daniels will take the run option every single time. We'll see if Parker will make the proper adjustments in week two.

articles.title: Promotion-chasing Northants trail against Derbyshire
articles.summary: Northamptonshire are bowled out for 310 in the final over of day two at the County Ground and trail Derbyshire by 62 on first innings.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division Two, cinch County Ground, Northampton (day two)

Derbyshire 372: Madsen 151, Aitchison 106; Guthrie 3-66, Sanderson 3-72

Northamptonshire 310: Vasconcelos 58, Procter 54, McManus 53; Randell 3-48

Northants (5 pts) trail Derbyshire (6 pts) by 62 runs

Derbyshire's New Zealand seamer Brett Randell led the charge with 3-48 as Northamptonshire were dismissed for 310, trailing by 62 runs, on an attritional second day at Wantage Road.

Ricardo Vasconcelos made 58, passing 900 runs for the season in an opening partnership of 97 with Luke Procter (54), who was captaining Northamptonshire for the 50th time in Championship matches.

Saif Zaib scored a busy 46, but with Northamptonshire handily placed on 187-2 shortly before tea, injury substitute Nick Potts (3-51) took wickets with consecutive deliveries.

The promotion-hunting hosts' hopes were further dented after tea when Randell took two wickets in one over on a surface offering movement and bounce for seamers and spinners alike.

Luis Reece also took two, including his 200th first-class wicket for Derbyshire, as the hosts slumped to 243-8.

But Lewis McManus and Ben Sanderson (27) staged a late recovery with a flurry of boundaries to clinch two precious batting bonus points.

McManus was finally dismissed for 53, after passing 4,000 first-class runs.

Resuming on 15 without loss, Vasconcelos and Procter both found early runs through the covers off the seamers.

Vasconcelos passed 50 before driving Reece sweetly down the ground as Northamptonshire went into lunch on 96 without loss.

Ben Aitchison made the key breakthrough immediately after the interval, jagging one back to trap Vasconcelos lbw, but the Derbyshire all-rounder was later substituted following a suspected groin strain, Potts coming in as the official replacement.

Runs were in short supply for the first hour post-lunch as Mohammad Abbas and Randell beat the bat and found some sharp bounce.

The Northants skipper finally clipped one off his legs off Abbas for a welcome boundary before going to his half-century with a fluent straight drive off Randell. He fell shortly afterwards, though, lbw to Reece from a full delivery.

Zaib looked to play positively from the start, dancing down the wicket to deposit Bashir over midwicket. He took a liking to Martin Andersson too, pulling him behind square and smashing another delivery through the covers.

Gus Miller played more conservatively but collected two boundaries off the seamers. He was dropped on 18 by Wayne Madsen at first slip off Abbas, but his reprieve was brief as he pulled a short wide one from Potts to mid-wicket.

Northamptonshire's afternoon ended in disarray as Potts struck with his next delivery, Zaib playing another rash shot when he pulled a short leg-side delivery to fine-leg.

James Sales saw off the hat-trick ball after tea, but Randell struck with the second new ball, bowling full to trap Calvin Harrison lbw before moving one back five balls later to hit Sales' off stump."

McManus and George Bartlett garnered early boundaries, but as scoring dried up Northants lost two wickets in seven balls. First Bartlett nicked behind off Potts, then Liam Guthrie chipped to cover off Reece.

Sanderson and McManus entertained the crowd with a counterattack, Sanderson hitting Potts for six over deep mid-wicket before McManus pulled for six more.

Randell removed Sanderson but McManus continued to blaze boundaries, swivelling to pull one out of the ground over deep-midwicket before falling to Andersson in the day's final over.

articles.title: Liverpool Are Well Positioned To Land This Ligue 1 Midfielder In January: Good Choice For Iraola?
articles.summary: In a recent report, journalist Pete O’Rourke stated that Liverpool are well-positioned to land Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara this January. It has been ment...
articles.body:
In a recent report , journalist Pete O'Rourke stated that Liverpool are well-positioned to land Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara this January. It has been mentioned that the Reds are keeping a keen eye on the French talent ahead of a potential move for him in this winter transfer window.

Camara's Impressive Form In French Football

Camara enjoyed a good run of form at the French club in the previous campaign when he put in a series of impressive displays for them in the middle of the park. The 22-year-old scored three times and earned four assists in 31 matches for Monaco last season on all fronts.

The French talent is currently among the most gifted central midfielders in Ligue 1. Hence, it is no surprise that the Reds are showing interest in recruiting him this January.

His current contract at Monaco will run out in the summer of 2029, which could make it tough for Liverpool to sign him on a cut-price deal in this winter transfer window.

SEATTLE, WASHINGTON – JULY 01: Lamine Camara of Senegal in action during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Round Of 32 match between Belgium and Senegal at Seattle Stadium on July 01, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

Will Camara Be A Good Choice For Liverpool Boss Andoni Iraola ?

Camara is a good tackler of the ball and can read the danger well to earn possession back for his team inside his half. He usually puts his foot through the ball when needed and can chip in by scoring and creating a few important goals for his team from midfield.

The French sensation is primarily a box-to-box midfielder but can also serve as a defensive midfielder if asked to do so. However, it remains to be seen whether he can cope with the physical side and high intensity of the Premier League if the Reds manage to bring him on board this winter.

We can expect Camara to enhance the quality of Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola's midfield department. He is good enough to challenge for a regular first-team spot at the Merseyside club.

At 22, the future looks quite promising for Camara as long as he continues to improve with each year. He is already capable of helping the Reds challenge across all competitions over the next few years. All in all, Camara would be a decent choice for Liverpool to pursue in the January transfer window, but only if they can sign him for a reasonable price.

articles.title: ESPN re-signs Joe Buck for more than $100 million, highlighting company strategy
articles.summary: Joe Buck's new six-year, $108 million ESPN extension secures him through the 2031 Super Bowl, but Troy Aikman's own contract remains unsigned.
articles.body: ESPN and Joe Buck have agreed to a six-year contract extension worth around $108 million. The deal will raise Buck’s annual salary from $15 million to $18 million, as The Athletic first reported Wednesday. Buck signed with ESPN in 2022 alongside his longtime broadcast partner, Troy Aikman. In terms of scale, signing Buck and Aikman marked one of ESPN’s most important talent acquisitions in its 40-year history. The network spent years trying to find a booth that could match the quality of its competitors, from Sean McDonough and Steve Levy to Booger McFarland and Jason Witten. Those pairings did not work. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Buck and Aikman do. In fact, they are often considered the best game duo in all of sports. Aikman, who signed a five-year, $90 million contract with ESPN, remains unsigned. His contract expires after the Super Bowl in February. We expect him to re-sign. Buck’s new deal secures him for not only the upcoming Super Bowl but also ESPN’s next one in 2031. At 57, Buck could be in line for another contract after this one. For context, Al Michaels still calls Thursday Night Football for Amazon Prime at 81. JOSH PATE DISCUSSES NEW ESPN SHOW, FOUR FACES OF ESPN, PAT MCAFEE AND FUTURE OF MEDIA COMPANY WITH OUTKICK Joe Buck is now tied with Aikman as ESPN’s third-highest-paid on-air personality, behind Stephen A. Smith and Pat McAfee. Smith makes around $21 million per year, while McAfee makes around $30 million. Note: McAfee’s deal is not a standard talent contract. He licenses his daily studio show to the network and has a separate agreement that includes roles on "College GameDay," "Monday Night Countdown," and other ESPN appearances. McAfee is reportedly in contract discussions with ESPN on a renewal worth around $65 million per year. The deals for Buck, McAfee, Aikman, and Smith highlight ESPN’s strategy under chairman Jimmy Pitaro. The stars get paid. The middle class does not. Renewals for those four personalities come as ESPN laid off multiple on-air talents in July, following another round of layoffs that affected 20 on-air talents in 2023. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Other ESPN talents in the "star" category include Michael Wilbon, Tony Kornheiser, Kirk Herbstreit, and Mike Breen. Considering the value of calling a Super Bowl, Buck might be the most valuable of them. Buck could also return to calling the World Series if ESPN adds the event to its portfolio in 2029. According to The Athletic, Pitaro has told Buck he would like him to call the World Series if ESPN adds it. The World Series is currently exclusive to FOX, where Buck long called the event, but could be split between multiple broadcast partners in the next rights negotiations. FOX, ESPN, NBC, and Netflix are among the likely bidders.

articles.title: Duras críticas a Luis Díaz en su peor momento en el Bayern: "El rey de las ocasiones desperdiciadas"
articles.standfirst: El colombiano atraviesa un difícil momento en Alemania mientras recibe cuestionamientos por su rendimiento
articles.summary: El colombiano atraviesa un difícil momento en Alemania mientras recibe cuestionamientos por su rendimiento
articles.body: El extremo colombiano Luis Díaz se encuentra en el centro del debate deportivo en Alemania. El jugador guajiro vive un arranque de temporada marcado por la irregularidad y la falta de definición de cara al arco rival, lo que ha generado duras críticas en los medios locales, molestia entre sus compañeros en el terreno de juego y cuestionamientos por parte de la afición en redes sociales. El diario Bild, uno de los periódicos de mayor circulación en Alemania, publicó un informe bajo el título “La frustración estalla para la estrella del Bayern”. En el artículo se detalla una jugada ocurrida durante el triunfo 2-1 ante el SV Elversberg. Al minuto 67, con el marcador igualado 1-1, Díaz recibió una asistencia precisa de Michael Olise en el centro del área. Sin embargo, tras un mal control de balón, intentó un remate de tacón que terminó suavemente en manos del guardameta rival. La acción desencadenó la reacción evidente de su compañero Josip Stanišić, quien mostró su enojo de forma visible en el campo. Por su parte, el portal especializado Fussball Europa reaccionó con un titular contundente: “Luis Díaz, el rey de las ocasiones desperdiciadas: ¿FC Bayern cometió un error?”. El medio cuestionó la baja tasa de conversión del colombiano, destacando que su registro de anotaciones no refleja la cantidad de opciones claras generadas. En declaraciones a la prensa internacional, Díaz señaló que la falta del mejor ritmo colectivo responde a la exigente seguidilla de partidos acumulada desde la campaña anterior y la recargada agenda internacional. "Todavía no estamos en ese nivel, pero creo que eso es normal. Es normal porque hemos tenido una carga de trabajo pesada. Hemos jugado un número increíble de partidos importantes en los últimos meses... Muchos de nosotros también estuvimos en el Mundial después. Luego tienes comparativamente poco tiempo de descanso", señaló el jugador colombiano. Pese a que el atacante apenas registra un gol en el arranque del curso oficial, el colombiano resaltó la importancia de mantener la tranquilidad mientras la plantilla recupera su punto óptimo de rendimiento físico y futbolístico. A pesar de los cuestionamientos de la prensa y las plataformas digitales, el cuerpo técnico y la directiva del club bávaro mantienen la confianza en el atacante colombiano. Max Eberl, directivo de la institución, dio muestras de apoyo a Lucho en sus declaraciones a los medios tras el encuentro frente al Elversberg: "¿Qué soy yo, como defensor que nunca ha marcado un gol, para decirle a Lucho Díaz cómo puede mejorar su definición? Lucho no tiene el ritmo en este momento". El club confía en que con el correr de los partidos y la suma de minutos, el atacante recupere el nivel de definición y el ritmo de juego que lo han caracterizado a lo largo de su carrera.
